chunks: (So had We destroyed) the people of Noah before them: They were surely a sinful people.
ai.seo_question: Who were the people of Noah and why were they considered sinful?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the collective moral decay of Noah's people, characterizing them as 'fasiqeen' (transgressors) who rejected divine authority despite clear signs. Their destruction serves as a primordial archetype for the consequences of persistent disbelief and social corruption, a theme frequently echoed in the narrative of the Ahl al-Bayt's struggles against their contemporaries.
